physics.astrophysics-cosmology-explain-k.all: Galaxy moving away stretches wavelength (Doppler effect); greater change in wavelength = greater speed, v = c*dlambda/lambda0

physics.astrophysics-cosmology-extended-.a: Universe began from a single very small, very hot, dense point/ region and has been expanding since
physics.astrophysics-cosmology-extended-.b: Plan: universe began ~13.8 bn yr ago from tiny hot dense point, expanded and cooled. Evidence: red-shift of distant galaxies - all receding; further galaxies greater red-shift so faster (expanding). CMB radiation - remnant of early hot universe, red-shifted to microwaves, uniform in all directions.

physics.astrophysics-cosmology-recall-kb.b: Universe began from a single small, hot, dense point and has expanded since

physics.astrophysics-stars-describe-kb.0.all: Main sequence: diagonal band top-left (hot, bright) to bottom-right (cool, dim); red giants: top right (cool, bright); white dwarfs: bottom left (hot, dim)

physics.astrophysics-stars-explain-kb.00.a: High surface temperature but very small surface area so low luminosity / emits little total light
physics.astrophysics-stars-explain-kb.00.b: Surface is relatively cool (~3000-4000 K); so peak emission at red end/ emits mostly red light

physics.astrophysics-stars-recall-kb.000.all: Absolute magnitude (or luminosity) and surface temperature (or colour/spectral class)

physics.astrophysics-universe-describe-k.a: Moon orbits a planet, planet orbits the Sun (star); moon orbit smaller radius/ shorter period
physics.astrophysics-universe-describe-k.b: Weight decreases (to about 1/6) because gravitational field strength smaller on the Moon; mass unchanged

physics.astrophysics-universe-explain-kb.a: Direction of velocity continually changes so velocity changes; acceleration towards centre due to gravity
physics.astrophysics-universe-explain-kb.b: Gravitational field strength smaller on Moon so smaller weight/ smaller downward force/deceleration; same take-off speed reaches greater height
physics.astrophysics-universe-explain-kb.c: Larger orbit so greater distance to travel per orbit; and weaker gravity so lower orbital speed

physics.electricity-charge-explain-kb.00.a: Current is rate of flow of electrons/charge; electrons not used up and only one path so same number pass each point per second
physics.electricity-charge-explain-kb.00.b: 1.5 J of energy transferred per coulomb of charge (passing through the cell)

physics.electricity-circuits-describe-kb.a: No current in reverse direction (very high resistance); in forward direction little current until ~0.6-0.7 V threshold, then current rises steeply
physics.electricity-circuits-describe-kb.b: Straight line through origin; I proportional to V so V/I constant
physics.electricity-circuits-describe-kb.c: Slider changes length of wire/resistance in circuit; increasing resistance decreases current (and vice versa)

physics.electricity-circuits-explain-kb..a: Thermistor resistance decreases as temperature rises; so current increases / voltage changes to trigger switch for fan
physics.electricity-circuits-explain-kb..b: LDR resistance increases as light level falls (dark); this change triggers the circuit to switch lights on
physics.electricity-circuits-explain-kb..c: Larger current heats the filament; atoms/ions vibrate more; more collisions with electrons so higher resistance

physics.electricity-circuits-extended-kb.a: If one lamp breaks the others stay on (or each gets full voltage / switched independently)
physics.electricity-circuits-extended-kb.b: Plan: LDR in potential divider; in dark LDR resistance rises so its voltage share rises, triggering switch/relay to turn lamps on. Thermistor (NTC) in second potential divider; when cold its resistance rises so voltage across it rises, triggering switch for heater. Fixed/variable resistor sets threshold; reverse when bright/warm.

physics.electricity-circuits-mcq-kb.0012.a: each lamp can be switched on and off independently

physics.electricity-mains-describe-kb.00.a: Fuse in live wire; if current exceeds rating the wire heats and melts; breaks circuit, stopping current (preventing fire/overheating)
physics.electricity-mains-describe-kb.00.b: Plastic/insulating case so live parts cannot touch accessible parts; user cannot get electric shock even if a wire comes loose

physics.electricity-mains-explain-kb.000.a: Electrons collide with ions/atoms in the resistor; transferring energy, making ions vibrate more so temperature rises
physics.electricity-mains-explain-kb.000.b: Plastic is an insulator; case cannot become live so no shock risk (earth not needed)

physics.electricity-mains-extended-kb.00.b: Plan: I = P/V = 2000/230 = 8.7 A; choose fuse just above normal current: 13 A (3 A and 5 A would blow in normal use). Too large a fuse: fault current may not melt it, wires overheat, fire risk/shock. Fuse in live wire.

physics.electricity-mains-mcq-kb.0005.all: has a plastic case and does not need an earth wire

physics.electricity-static-explain-kb.00.all: Friction transfers electrons; electrons move from jumper to balloon so balloon has excess electrons

physics.electricity-static-extended-kb.0.b: Plan: rub two polythene rods with cloth, suspend one; bring other close - repel. Rub acetate rod, bring to polythene - attract. So two types. Polythene gains electrons (negative); acetate loses electrons (positive). Like charges repel, unlike attract.

physics.electricity-static-mcq-kb.0004.all: charge flows through the metal and the person to earth
